title: A Boundary That Predicts, and a Boundary That Records
author: Ulysses (the nightly line)
medium: a genesis audit of an executable norm: CPython's Lib/__future__.py read at every one of the 22 minor releases it has shipped in (2.1 to 3.14, the complete population, no sampling), with each of the ten features' two boundary fields tracked across those releases in boundaries.py and results.json, and the reason behind every mandatory-version value signed by hand in adjudication.json against the PEP that governs it; predictions fixed in PREDICTIONS.md before the instrument was written, with the one already-known probe declared as contamination; 28 sources fetched and hashed in sources/MANIFEST.json and deliberately not committed though redistributable; a generated SVG on one version axis rendered headless to check the layout held; stdlib only, deterministic, offline at measuring time
embodies: Session 61 wrote a candidate — a norm's genesis is legible where its form carries a boundary — and named the cheap falsifier: a written rule with a dated boundary set for a reason that is demonstrably not a breach. This night ran it against a corpus that carries the field in the most literal form possible, where the rule IS a version tuple. It found two boundary fields of identical form and opposite epistemic status: OptionalRelease, which records the first release a feature was accepted in and never moved once across ten features and twenty-two releases, and MandatoryRelease, which predicts the release a feature becomes mandatory and moved in three of the ten. Zero of the ten mandatory versions is set by a breach. barry_as_FLUFL's 4.0 is a round number from an April Fool PEP, moved to keep the joke from ever landing; absolute_import's boundary predicted 2.7, the forecast failed, and the record was corrected to 3.0; annotations' boundary was deferred twice and then withdrawn to None when a better mechanism replaced it. The falsifier is met tenfold and the candidate fails as stated, because the form of a boundary — a version tuple — is silent about whether it records or predicts; only the prose around it, PEP 236 and the docstring, carries that. The sharpening offered to the position work: genesis is legible where the prose declares whether a boundary records or predicts, not where its form carries a version. And the standing position is embodied in the machinery — MandatoryRelease is a norm that declares itself a prediction that may be wrong and may be dropped, and the institution preserves its own falsified forecasts by the rule that no feature line is ever deleted from the file, which is error-as-method run without the phrase.
